introduction: On this Sunday, Moses pleads with God for his people after they worship the golden calf, and God relents. In the Gospel, Jesus tells three parables of mercy: the shepherd who searches for the lost sheep, the woman who searches for the lost coin, and the father who welcomes his lost son. Paul says, Christ came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost. Let us rejoice in God's mercy.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. Let us bring our prayers to the merciful Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may go out to search for the lost with the patience of the woman with the lamp. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have strayed from God: that they may discover that heaven rejoices when they return. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who intercede for others, like Moses: that their prayers may obtain mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who think they are too sinful to be forgiven: that they may learn from Saint Paul that no one is beyond God's mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may rejoice when sinners return, and not grumble like the elder brother. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Merciful Father, you search for the lost and rejoice when they are found. Have mercy on us sinners, and make us share your joy over every person who comes home. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Rejoice with me
reflection.body:
While Moses is on the mountain with God, the people make a golden calf and worship it. God is ready to destroy them. But Moses intercedes. He reminds God of his promises to Abraham, Isaac and Israel. And "the LORD turned away from the evil which he said he would do to his people." The prayer of one person can change the course of events.

In the Gospel, the Pharisees and scribes grumble that Jesus welcomes sinners and eats with them. Jesus answers with three parables about lost things, and they all end in joy.

A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep to search for the one that is lost, and carries it home on his shoulders. A woman who has ten silver coins loses one. She lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and searches carefully until she finds it. Then she calls her friends: "Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!" Jesus says, "Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting."

The third parable is the story of the father and his two sons. The father runs to embrace the son who returns, and he goes out to plead with the son who refuses to come in.

In all three parables, God is the one who searches. We are precious to him, like the coin the woman will not stop looking for. And when the lost are found, heaven celebrates.

Paul knows this mercy personally. He was "a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent," yet he received mercy. So he writes: "Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief." No one is beyond God's reach.

This week, let God find you, through prayer and confession. And when someone returns to the faith or to the community, rejoice with heaven and make them welcome.
